textRuns.value: Global figures are the source's own World series, which includes international transport. Country figures exclude it, along with continents, income groups and alternative source series, so the 233 countries sum to 97.2% of the world total rather than 100%.

Coal's share of emissions has fallen steadily since 1900, but its volume has not. Global coal emissions rose from 8,689 Mt in 1990 to 14,980 in 2021, a 72% increase. A falling share and a rising quantity are not in conflict, and no chart on this page shows the second one.

The dip at 2020 is the largest single-year fall on record at 1,818 Mt, more than double the fall at the end of the Second World War. As a percentage, at 4.9%, it does not reach the top six. It was erased within twelve months: 2021 finished above 2019.
